conventions.unverified: The literal string 'unverified' (and the top-level 'unverified' list) means no fetched source stated the value. Nothing was guessed, averaged, interpolated or filled from memory.
conventions.src: Every entry carries 'src', a list of ids in the top-level 'sources' array, plus a 'location' (page, table, section).
conventions.quotes: 'quote' strings are verbatim from pdftotext output, HTML-to-text, or RTF-to-text. Line breaks and hyphenation were joined and runs of spaces collapsed; pdftotext spacing artifacts are kept. Non-English quotes keep the original language; 'gloss_en' is the research agent's translation. Quotes flagged 'from_image' were read from a picture.
conventions.quote_check: The build script searched every quote not flagged 'from_image' in the saved text of its cited source (whitespace-insensitive, Unicode NFKC); 'quote_check' records the result. For sources gathered by the sub-agents (B16.9 catalogs, European documents) the search covers all saved text in that sub-agent's download folder.
conventions.transcription: Tables were parsed programmatically from pdftotext -layout output and cross-checked across editions where several exist (DOE Tip #17 2004/2006/2012; Illinois TRM v8.0/v15.0; B16.9 tables across 2-4 catalogs). Small values were hand-transcribed and token-checked. 'printed' fields keep the source strings.
conventions.equivalent_length: An 'equivalent length' is the length of straight pipe whose heat loss (or, in most sources, whose outside surface area) equals that of the fitting. Each entry says what it is equivalent to: bare pipe of the same size, insulated pipe, or pipe of a stated size. Area-based equivalents (Illinois TRM, F6, NGRID) assume the fitting surface loses heat at the same rate per unit area as the pipe; DOE Tip #17-derived values (NIA 2008) are energy-based.
conventions.agent_checks: Values under methods_notes 'agent_consistency_checks' were computed by the research agent from the sourced numbers. They are cross-checks only.
conventions.marketing: Vendor sources are flagged MARKETING. Vendor numbers without a cited basis are listed under 'unverified' only.

conventions.pipe_dimensions: NPS-to-OD values are in research/pipe-dimensions.json and are not repeated here.

methods_notes.topic: agent_consistency_checks
methods_notes.label: COMPUTED BY THE RESEARCH AGENT FROM THE SOURCED VALUES. Cross-checks only, not source values.

checks.check: Illinois TRM equivalent length vs (printed area) / (pi x pipe OD / 12)
checks.result: All 50 printed equivalent lengths (18 elbow/tee, 32 valve/flange) equal the printed surface area divided by the outside surface of 1 ft of bare steel pipe of the same NPS, to within 0.011 ft (rounding of the printed areas). So the TRM equivalent lengths are bare-OD-area equivalents.

checks.check: Illinois TRM elbow/tee surface areas vs ASME B16.9 geometry
checks.result: Straight tee: the TRM area equals pi x OD x 3C (C = B16.9 tee center-to-end from fitting_dimensions) to within 0.007 ft2 for NPS 1-12, i.e. three pipe stubs of length C. 90-degree elbow: the TRM area is 1.48 to 1.88 times the side area of a long-radius torus segment (pi x OD x (pi/2) x A, A = B16.9 LR center-to-end); the ratio grows with NPS. The TRM elbow formula therefore does not match B16.9 long-radius centerline geometry and its basis is unknown.

checks.check: F6 C1129 values vs Illinois TRM valve areas
checks.result: F6's NPS 6 class 150 (7.03 ft2) and class 300 (9.71 ft2) C1129 Table 1 values are the same numbers as the F12 valve-area cells, and F6's 5.6 / 4.05 LF equal those areas divided by pi x 6.625/12 ft to the printed precision.

Deemed therms per fitting / therms per foot = 37.56/10.58 (2026) and 40.44/11.38 (2023); both ratios round to 3.55, matching the stated equivalent length. No source is given for 3.55 ft; it is numerically close to the F12 NPS 2 class 150 valve value (3.56 ft) but the WI TRM does not say so.

checks.check: National Grid 2014 gate-valve equivalences vs C1129
checks.result: F19 gives 5.2 LF for an NPS 6 class 150 gate valve while the C1129-based value is 4.05 LF (F6) - about 28% higher; the slide gives no area or dimensions, so the difference cannot be traced.
